qt: to the Commission Valentina Palmisano (The Left), Mario Furore (The Left), Pasquale Tridico (The Left), Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Gaetano Pedulla' (The Left), Carolina Morace (The Left) Subject:

The Coratina cultivar – the epitome of Puglian olive growing – produces a quality extra virgin oil which, due to its natural characteristics, can have a sterol content below the EU threshold of 1 000 mg/kg. By means of Decision (EU) 2026/711, the Council of the European Union supported the inclusion of Coratina1 in the derogation for the Koroneiki and Nocellara del Belice varieties. On 1 July 2026, the International Olive Council subsequently approved the minimum threshold of 800 mg/kg for Coratina as well. However, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2358 did not include Coratina. According to producer organisations2, the exclusion can apparently be traced back to the start of the EU process before the International Olive Council’s decision. The failure to transpose the derogation risks causing the downgrading and devaluation of legitimate oils, with serious consequences for producers, mills and Puglia’s provinces in the 2026-2027 marketing year. In light of the above: 1.

What prevented Coratina from being included in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2358? Is this exclusion due to the time lag between the EU legislative process and the decision made by the International Olive Council?
Will the Commission amend Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2358 as a matter of urgency and extend the minimum threshold of 800 mg/kg to Coratina from the next oil marketing year?
